circularity_adjudication.question: The fixtures use a DATA statement to lay values down in array element order, then read back by subscript. Is that circular, given that 9.5.3.3 is itself the definition of array element order?
circularity_adjudication.reasoning: 9.5.3.3 owns the element-order formula and the sequence. The DATA statement, specified in 8.6.7, is a legitimate CONSUMER of that ordering rather than a restatement of it. The expected values are independently hand-computed literal constants, not values derived by the mechanism under test, and the read-back is by subscript, which is independent of the ordering mechanism.
circularity_adjudication.excluded_mechanisms: No fixture establishes order via RESHAPE, PACK, TRANSFER, sequence association, or any storage-layout assumption.

non_vacuity_by_mutation.principle: A case that still passes when the thing it tests is broken establishes nothing. Inspection is not sufficient evidence of non-vacuity; mutation is.
mutation_classes: same-multiset value swaps - catches an oracle that checks only the set of values rather than their positions
unit-lower-bound mutation - catches an off-by-one that a unit lower bound would hide
non_vacuity_by_mutation.verdict: all 13 mutations produced a failing test, so the fixtures are demonstrably not vacuous

design_for_discrimination.non_unit_lower_bounds: every array uses them, so an off-by-one in the formula cannot hide
design_for_discrimination.distinct_extents: the rank-two arrays have distinct extents, so a transposed formula is caught
design_for_discrimination.interior_subscripts: the exercised subscripts are away from the first and last elements, where a wrong formula can still coincidentally agree
design_for_discrimination.coordinate_coded_literals: element values encode their own subscripts, so reading a position identifies unambiguously which element is there
